svg.title: Spark shuffle internals: the write path, the read path, and why it pins executors
svg.desc: Spark shuffle internals in Microsoft Fabric: Wide transformation stage cuts, Map-side data and index file writes to local disk, driver MapOutputTracker cataloging, reduce-side parallel block fetching, executor pinning, FetchFailedException recompute, and the three mitigation strategies.
svg.text: Spark Shuffle Internals — Write Path, Read Path & Executor Pinning
Stage boundaries ➔ Map data/index disk writes ➔ MapOutputTracker ➔ Parallel reduce fetches ➔ The 3 scale-down solutions
LANE 1: MAP-SIDE SHUFFLE WRITE & METADATA REGISTRATION

g.title: Wide transformation — A wide transformation forces redistribution and starts a new stage.
Map task writes its output — Each map task writes one data file and one index file of partition offsets.
g.text: • Emits 1 Data File per task containing
• Emits 1 Index File per task holding
exact byte offsets for every bucket

g.title: …to executor-local disk — Shuffle output is written once to executor-local disk with no replica.
g.text: • Data lands on local executor disk
• No Replication: Stored only on the
specific VM node that generated it
• Executor becomes an active file server

g.title: MapOutputTracker — The driver's MapOutputTracker maps shuffle partitions to block locations.

svg.text: LANE 2: REDUCE-SIDE FETCH, PINNING & THE RECOMPUTE CASCADE

g.title: Reduce task fetches blocks — Reduce tasks fetch their blocks in parallel from every producing executor.
g.text: • Fetches block partition slices in parallel
• Buffers in memory; spills if limit exceeded

g.aria-label: So the producer cannot be released
g.title: So the producer cannot be released — An executor holding unread shuffle output cannot be safely released.
g.text: • Idle ≠ Safe to Remove: 0 tasks does not
• Later stages still need its local shuffle files
• Releasing node destroys only copy of data
• You pay for idle compute to protect data

g.title: Remove it anyway → stage recompute — A failed fetch recomputes the entire owning stage, not one partition.

svg.text: LANE 3: THE THREE ARCHITECTURAL SOLUTIONS TO BREAK THE COUPLING

g.title: The bond to break — Shuffle output living and dying with its executor is the bond to break.
Shuffle tracking — Shuffle tracking keeps executors holding needed shuffle data alive.
g.text: but still pays for idle nodes

g.title: External shuffle service — An external shuffle service serves shuffle files beyond the executor's lifetime.
Graceful decommissioning — Graceful decommissioning migrates blocks to a peer before the executor exits.

svg.text: Fabric Atlas — Original Diagram, August 2026. Sourced from Apache Spark Architecture & Microsoft Fabric Efficient Scaledown docs.
